The shell runner is currently being blocked by the sandbox before it can even do read-only searches. I’m going to use the available MCP/resource path next, and if that also isn’t exposed I’ll give you the mapping framework explicitly with the assumptions called out.

I can map them, but I’m blocked from reading the repo right now: every shell command, including `pwd` and `rg`, is failing before execution with:


Given that, here’s a clean parent-issue-to-gates map you can use as the working structure. I’m treating “parent issue” as an epic-level implementation theme, and “gates” as the required checks before a change can be considered safe to ship.

| Parent Issue | Build Gate | Test Gate | Drift Gate | Routing Gate | Rollback Gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Skill authoring / improvement flow | `./bin/ask repo doctor --json --robot` passes; skill source compiles or validates through repo wrapper; no edits to runtime projections | `./bin/ask skills prove <handle> --json --robot`; focused fixture or golden-output tests for changed skill behavior | Verify canonical skill source and projected/runtime copies are in sync; no unauthorized edits under generated/runtime paths; line-budget and frontmatter conventions preserved | Confirm skill handle resolves through `./bin/ask skills explain <handle> --json --robot`; discovery metadata routes the right user intent to the skill | Revert only changed canonical skill files; retain prior skill version or generated projection; document restored handle/version |
| Skill discovery / registry / marketplace metadata | Registry generation/build command passes through `./bin/ask`; metadata schema validates; no duplicate handles | Query/discovery tests prove skill appears under expected search terms and does not shadow unrelated skills | Compare registry output against canonical skill metadata; detect stale generated marketplace/runtime entries | Validate route from user phrasing to skill handle, category, plugin, or marketplace entry; check aliases and descriptions | Restore previous registry/marketplace entry; remove new aliases if routing is noisy; re-run discovery proof |
| Policy / AGENTS / operator docs updates | Docs validation or repo doctor passes; links resolve where tooling supports it | If docs drive automation, run corresponding robot command examples; otherwise use targeted smoke checks for referenced workflows | Check contradictions against `UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md`, path ownership docs, and existing AGENTS scopes | Confirm docs point agents to the correct wrapper commands, package roots, and ownership paths | Revert doc sections independently; preserve any unrelated guidance; include exact removed/changed policy text in closeout |
| Runtime projection / sync pipeline | Sync/build command succeeds through repo wrapper; generated artifacts are reproducible | Snapshot/golden tests for projection output; prove changed source produces expected runtime result | Diff canonical source against projection output; fail on manual projection edits or stale generated files | Validate projected path is discoverable by the intended runtime, plugin, or skill loader | Regenerate from last known canonical source; avoid hand-editing projection files; restore previous projection artifact if needed |
| Repo command / `./bin/ask` control plane | `./bin/ask repo doctor --json --robot` passes; wrapper works from repo root | Unit/integration tests for command behavior; JSON robot output is parseable and stable | Ensure root wrappers still forward to `Infrastructure/bin/ask`; no divergence between documented and actual commands | Verify subcommand routing, flags, and `--robot` mode select the intended handler | Restore previous command implementation or wrapper; keep backwards-compatible aliases if users depend on them |
| Validation / closeout workflow | Required build commands complete before closeout; changed-file scope is known | Required skill proofs, package tests, or smoke checks pass with explicit evidence | `./bin/ask repo closeout --changed --json --robot` reports no unexpected drift; generated files accounted for | Confirm closeout routes each changed path to the right ownership and validation expectations | If validation fails late, revert or isolate only the failing change; preserve passing unrelated changes |
| Package-root implementation work | Build command runs only inside verified package root; no root-level package-manager install | Package-local tests plus repo-level doctor where relevant | Check lockfile/package metadata changes are intentional and scoped; no root/package boundary violations | Confirm imports, package scripts, and wrappers route through the intended package root | Restore package-local files and lockfile changes together; avoid partial dependency rollback |
| Agent-facing workflow / routing docs | Docs/build checks pass; examples use current command syntax | Scenario tests or manual command probes prove agents can follow the workflow | Compare workflow docs against `Docs/agents/*`, AGENTS.md, and `UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md` for stale terms | Validate task phrasing routes to the intended skill/plugin/doc path; avoid ambiguous overlapping triggers | Remove or narrow new routing language; restore previous workflow wording if agents misroute |
| Security / permissions / safety guidance | Static/docs checks pass; no unsafe command examples introduced | Negative-path tests or review checks cover forbidden destructive operations and approval behavior | Check guidance against current sandbox, approval, and path ownership policy | Confirm safety instructions route risky work to the correct security/review workflow | Revert risky guidance immediately; restore stricter prior policy text; document residual risk |
| CI / automation / generated checks | CI config validates; local equivalent build passes where available | CI job/unit tests pass; robot JSON remains machine-consumable | Detect config drift between local wrapper behavior and CI invocation | Confirm CI triggers on the right paths and selects the correct jobs for skills/docs/runtime changes | Revert CI config separately from product changes; disable only the bad job/rule if needed and document follow-up |

A more compact way to apply this per parent issue:

| Gate | What It Must Prove |
|---|---|
| Build | The changed surface can be generated, compiled, validated, or loaded using repo-approved commands. |
| Test | The behavior that motivated the parent issue is covered by focused proof, not only broad repo health. |
| Drift | Canonical sources, generated projections, docs, and registry metadata have not silently diverged. |
| Routing | The right user intent, command, skill handle, path owner, or runtime loader reaches the changed artifact. |
| Rollback | There is a minimal, path-scoped way to undo the change without damaging unrelated user work. |

For this repo specifically, the default gate spine should usually be:

```bash
./bin/ask repo doctor --json --robot
./bin/ask skills explain <handle> --json --robot
./bin/ask skills prove <handle> --json --robot
./bin/ask repo closeout --changed --json --robot
```

Use `skills explain` as the routing gate, `skills prove` as the behavioral test gate, `repo closeout --changed` as the drift/evidence gate, and `repo doctor` as the broad build/repo-health gate. Rollback is path-scoped: revert only the canonical files touched for the parent issue, then regenerate or re-prove rather than manually repairing runtime projections.

I couldn’t bind this to exact issue IDs or files because the sandbox is currently preventing all repo reads.
